rule: Skip genuine one-time comparisons and record exact-source why. Retain ordinary reusable wording, a teachable core, or uncertain form/sense on editorial hold. Approval here is a recommendation only; decisions and exclusion register remain unchanged.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A fast-moving current of new demands shaped the team's week.
rows.guideMeaning: A rapidly changing force that is hard to resist; the water image describes modern life.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The water-current image is productive for rapidly changing pressures, and “fast-moving current” is ordinary usable wording. A single tailored demands sentence does not prove the target itself is one-time.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Check whether a narrower current-of-demands target is teachable or links to an existing current/tide owner.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Quiet reading can be oxygen for the mind after a difficult week.
rows.guideMeaning: Something essential for mental refreshment; oxygen is a vivid figurative comparison.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: This exact reading-as-oxygen-for-the-mind pairing is an invented life-support comparison. It offers no distinct conventional turn beyond ordinary “essential for mental refreshment.”
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Record the full source sentence and this reason; do not exclude “oxygen” or other independent expressions.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A good conversation can feel like fresh air for the mind.
rows.guideMeaning: Mental relief and renewal; fresh air is used figuratively.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The sentence explicitly says conversation can “feel like” fresh air for the mind. This is a tailored mental-relief simile, not the established “a breath of fresh air” expression.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Record the full comparison only; keep any separately sourced breath-of-fresh-air idiom.

rows.expression: all fireworks and not much substance
rows.exactGuideSentence: The speech was all fireworks and not much substance.
rows.guideMeaning: Exciting in appearance but shallow in content; fireworks is a figurative spectacle.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: “All fireworks and not much substance” may be a reusable spectacle-versus-content contrast built on the productive all-X/no-Y frame. The one sentence does not justify excluding that contrast without owner/form review.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Compare a bounded all-style/no-substance owner; do not silently collapse or exclude the fireworks wording.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The writer can introduce a minor theme and make it bloom much later.
rows.guideMeaning: Allow an early detail to become significant later; a growth metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: A writer introducing a minor theme and making “it bloom much later” is a single botanical image for narrative development. The full wording is not an independent conventional expression.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Record this exact writer/theme image; evaluate ordinary bloom/grow uses separately.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The final clue gave the audience a jolt of electricity.
rows.guideMeaning: A sudden intense shock or excitement; an electrical image.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: “A jolt of electricity” is an ordinary collocation and the source figuratively applies a sudden jolt to an audience. Its literal/figurative boundary merits target review rather than one-time exclusion.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Check whether a jolt-of-excitement owner or a bounded figurative electricity use is appropriate.

rows.expression: work now follows them home like a shadow
rows.exactGuideSentence: For some staff, work now follows them home like a shadow.
rows.guideMeaning: Job demands continue after people leave work; an extended shadow simile.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The full “like a shadow” simile is tailored, but “work follows them home” is a clear reusable core for after-hours intrusion. Excluding the whole source would discard that teachable wording.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Screen an owner for work following someone home; keep the shadow as source-specific imagery.

rows.expression: feel like a leash rather than a tool
rows.exactGuideSentence: Constant notifications can feel like a leash rather than a tool.
rows.guideMeaning: Feel controlling instead of helpful; a vivid comparison.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Notifications feeling “like a leash rather than a tool” is an explicit paired image made for this argument. The extracted full comparison is not a stable lexical target.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Record exact source; revisit any independent leash/control idiom if another source supports it.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Trust between them felt like a delicate thread.
rows.guideMeaning: Something fragile that can break under pressure; a thread metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: “A delicate thread” can describe a fragile relationship and the trust/thread pairing has broader transferable use. The source simile alone is insufficient to label the core one-time.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Review a bounded delicate-thread/trust owner and distinguish it from “hanging by a thread.”

rows.exactGuideSentence: Small kindnesses often land quietly in the heart.
rows.guideMeaning: Cause a private emotional effect; landing is figurative.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Kindnesses “land quietly in the heart” is a self-contained poetic personification; the exact adverbial landing-in-heart image does not supply a clear reusable unit.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Record the exact kindness/heart sentence, without excluding ordinary land-with-impact constructions.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Knowing the address gives you an internal backup system.
rows.guideMeaning: Knowledge kept in memory in case devices fail; a computing metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: “Backup system” is ordinary reusable wording, and applying it to memorised information may be a productive technology analogy. The current sentence does not establish that the whole phrase is merely one-time.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Check whether an internal-backup metaphor is natural across contexts before selecting or excluding.

rows.expression: sharp like a scalpel, not blunt like a hammer
rows.exactGuideSentence: Good regulation should be sharp like a scalpel, not blunt like a hammer.
rows.guideMeaning: Precise rather than indiscriminate; a vivid paired comparison.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The exact scalpel-versus-hammer simile is tailored, but the precision-versus-blunt-instrument contrast recurs as a transferable rhetorical frame. Narrow exclusion would be premature.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Review a bounded scalpel-not-hammer/scalpel-not-sledgehammer target and source form.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Credit should not look like a limitless tap to a child.
rows.guideMeaning: A source that appears to provide endlessly; a water metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Credit “looking like a limitless tap” is an explicit, source-specific water-supply analogy for a child’s perception of money. The full extracted image is not a conventional expression.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Record exact source; do not exclude other ordinary limitless or tap uses.

rows.expression: a musical crossroads where nostalgia meets novelty
rows.exactGuideSentence: The festival is a musical crossroads where nostalgia meets novelty.
rows.guideMeaning: A culture combining old and new influences; an extended crossroads metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: This festival-as-musical-crossroads where nostalgia meets novelty is a composite scene-specific image, combining two metaphors for one festival rather than one stable expression.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Record the full festival sentence; evaluate a separately sourced crossroads or where-X-meets-Y construction independently.

rows.exactGuideSentence: We should not drag every child through it by the arm.
rows.guideMeaning: Force participation instead of inviting it; an extended physical image.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: “Drag every child through it” contains the productive figurative drag-someone-through construction, even though “by the arm” extends the physical picture. Exclusion would lose a reusable force-participation meaning.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Review a bounded drag-someone-through owner and treat “by the arm” as source-specific detail.

rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Record this exact aphorism; keep separately sourced closed-door/open-window expressions distinct.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The hit became part of the cultural weather that summer.
rows.guideMeaning: A trend that shapes the shared atmosphere; a weather metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: “Cultural weather” can name a shared cultural atmosphere beyond this hit-song sentence; the image is potentially reusable in arts commentary. Do not infer one-time status from a single example.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Check register and overlap with cultural-climate/zeitgeist owners before deciding.

rows.exactGuideSentence: News has started living in people's pockets.
rows.guideMeaning: Become constantly available on phones; a spatial metaphor.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: “News in people’s pockets” is a reusable mobile-availability idea; “started living” personifies it in the source. The core remains teachable, so a one-time exclusion of the whole row would be too broad.
rows.boundaryOrNextCheck: Review a bounded news-in-your-pocket expression and keep the living personification source-specific.
